description: Original bipartite_vertex_cover mod.rs and bounded models
state: Left adjacency rows G and right population R, combined vertices at most 1000000 and total stored edges at most 1000000; duplicate neighbors allowed.
cost: Matching O((L+R+E)*sqrt(L+R+1)) time plus O(L+R+E) reachability. O(L+R) auxiliary storage. Endpoint validation precedes indexed traversal; allocation failure is untyped.
forward: Delegate resource/endpoint validation and matching to Hopcroft-Karp. Let Z start at unmatched left vertices and close under unmatched L-to-R edges and matched R-to-L edges. Return sorted (L minus ZL, ZR). König equality makes the cover cardinality equal to maximum matching cardinality.
inverse: Universe: valid graph/count inputs crossed with candidate sorted vertex subsets, together with typed validation errors. Absent behaviors include any uncovered edge, size unequal to maximum matching size, an out-of-range/duplicate/unsorted member, or selecting ZL on the left instead of its complement. With fixed deterministic matching and closure Z, every pair except (L minus ZL,ZR) is absent. Invalid inputs cannot return a cover; resource errors precede endpoint errors. This is an exact source-derived specification with partial finite correspondence, not a proof.

For fixed cover (A,B), compatible antecedents are all bounded valid graphs whose deterministic alternating closure has ZL=L minus A and ZR=B; equivalently retain the matching/closure existential intermediate constrained by the actual deterministic Hopcroft-Karp traversal. Merely requiring A,B to cover edges is insufficient. Edge duplicates and extra isolated right vertices can have the same cover, so recovery is ambiguous. Empty graphs with zero or one right vertex both yield empty cover. Error fibers retain all graphs with the same first failing validation field.
limitations: Finite evidence, not proof; allocation failure unmodeled.
Partial syntax, no macro expansion or semantic AST.
